- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes unrealistically; apply downward bias or cap forecasts at 1.5x recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–50% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — if recent 18-day average is 1.8–2.0, forecast should not exceed 2.2 unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits to recent volatility; use 3-day moving average of history as baseline for correction.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” or sharp reversal after peak, model tends to overpredict recovery; apply “reversal buffer” — reduce forecast by 15–25% for 2–3 days post-reversal.
